name: Saints of the Ethiopian Tewahedo Church
note: Hub collective for the canonized saints, sages, and Solomonic-cycle figures of Ethiopian Tewahedo Christianity; analytic grouping per Munro-Hay.

name: The Nine Saints
note: Group of nine (largely Syriac/Roman) missionary monks who, c. late 5th-early 6th c., spread monasticism and consolidated Christianity in Aksumite Ethiopia; attested in Ethiopian synaxaria and discussed by Munro-Hay.

name: Frumentius (Abba Selama)
note: First bishop of Aksum, called Abba Selama 'Revealer of Light'; converted King Ezana and the Aksumite court in the 4th c.; consecrated by Athanasius of Alexandria. Attested by Rufinus and Athanasius; treated by Munro-Hay.

name: Abba Aregawi (Za-Mikael)
note: Best-known of the Nine Saints; traditional founder of Debre Damo monastery. Attested in Ethiopian hagiography; discussed by Munro-Hay.

name: Saint Yared
note: 6th-c. deacon credited with inventing Ethiopian sacred chant (zema) and its notation; central to Tewahedo liturgy. Attested in Ethiopian tradition; noted by Munro-Hay.

name: Tekle Haymanot
note: 13th-c. monastic saint, founder of Debre Libanos and a key figure in the Solomonic restoration; among the most venerated Ethiopian saints. Attested in his Gadl (hagiography).

name: Gebre Menfes Kidus (Abbo)
note: Popular Ethiopian hermit-saint ('Servant of the Holy Spirit'), associated with Mount Ziquala; legendary ascetic figure of Ethiopian hagiography.

name: Gebre Mesqel Lalibela
note: Zagwe king (c. 1181-1221) credited with the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela ('New Jerusalem'); canonized king-saint. Attested historically and in his Gadl; discussed by Munro-Hay.

name: Makeda, Queen of Sheba
note: Ethiopian name for the Queen of Sheba; in the Kebra Nagast she visits Solomon and bears Menelik I, founding the Solomonic line. Reception/expansion of the biblical Queen of Sheba (1 Kings 10). Homonym/parallel of the biblical Sheba figure.

name: Menelik I
dom: kingship; dynastic founding; the Ark tradition
note: Legendary son of Solomon and Makeda; founder of the Ethiopian Solomonic dynasty who, in the Kebra Nagast, brings the Ark of the Covenant from Jerusalem to Aksum.

name: The Tabot (Ark of the Covenant tradition)
note: The Ethiopian Ark tradition: the Tabot (altar-tablet) replicates the Ark of the Covenant believed, per the Kebra Nagast, to reside at Aksum; central cultic object of every Tewahedo church.
